title: GeoPark donates more than 2,700 musical instruments and traditional costumes to seven schools in Puerto Gaitan
summary: GeoPark has donated more than 2,700 musical instruments and traditional costumes to seven schools in Puerto Gaitan, benefiting over 5,400 students, teachers, and other members of the educational community, including the Sikuani ethnic population.
body_markdown:
**1.742 billion-peso project is the Company’s first Works for Taxes project in Meta**


GeoPark has donated more than 2,700 musical instruments and traditional costumes to seven schools in Puerto Gaitan, benefiting over 5,400 students, teachers, and other members of the educational community, including the Sikuani ethnic population.


The equipment includes 1,722 musical instruments and elements and 1,050 traditional costumes and is part of the first project the Company has carried out in Meta through Works for Taxes. With an investment of 1.742 billion pesos, the initiative was developed alongside the Territorial Renewal Agency, the Ministry of National Education, the Meta Governor’s Office, and the Puerto Gaitan City Hall. It aims to strengthen the artistic training of students and preserve the municipality’s cultural traditions.


The beneficiary schools are the San Rafael de Domo Planas educational institution, the Kuwei educational institution, the Alto Tscocobo, Kayuwinae, and Horizontes educational centers, and the Unuma and Vencedor Piriri indigenous educational centers. The donation is complemented by training 35 teachers in a virtual diploma course,


“Cultural Processes as a Contribution to Comprehensive Education for Peace and Reconciliation,” that strengthens the role of culture in coexistence and peacebuilding from the classroom.


“It fills me with happiness to know that our boys and girls and young people from Puerto Gaitan will have more opportunities to learn and keep our traditions alive. Being from the Llanos myself, I feel enormous pride in our culture and how beautiful it is to know that what we so love will continue to live on in new generations. Thanks to GeoPark for making this donation possible and for working closely with schools,” Meta governor Rafaela Cortes said.


“At GeoPark, we invest in education because comprehensive training opens opportunities, and culture is an essential part of that training. With these tools and costumes, students and teachers from Puerto Gaitan will be able to carry out artistic and musical projects born from the traditions and knowledge of their communities. Doing Works for Taxes projects in Meta allows us to turn part of our taxes into concrete opportunities for the municipalities hosting our operation,” GeoPark Nature and Neighbors Director Anibal Fernandez de Soto said.


In Works for Taxes projects, GeoPark works alongside national, regional, and local authorities to close social gaps and contribute to the development of the territories where it operates. GeoPark has carried out 10 such projects in Casanare and Putumayo since 2021 and extended its participation in the mechanism to Meta in 2025. The accumulated investment exceeds 58.1 billion pesos and benefits more than 30,000 inhabitants of eight municipalities in Colombia.


**ABOUT GEOPARK**


GeoPark (NYSE: GPRK) is an independent oil and gas exploration and production company with more than 20 years of operations across Latin America and a proven track record in value creation. Its two-pillar strategy aims to maximize its core platform in Colombia, where it is one of the main operators, and to build a new long-term growth engine in Vaca Muerta – one of the world’s largest unconventional fields – and Venezuela through starting to operate the Bare block.
